method: GGUF headers read with HTTP Range requests (HF) and, on odie, with gguf-names.py plus a header-only reader; no model data read. Sizes = numel x block bpw of each ggml type.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.engram: blk.1 and blk.14 engram_embd [256, 384016682] each (header), 196.61B params total

custom_q_syntax: ik_llama.cpp --custom-q "regex=type,...": comma-split, std::regex_search on the tensor name, first matching rule wins, so put layer-specific rules before the catch-all. A regex cannot contain a comma (no {m,n}); list layers as (0|1|2).

rules.rule: Keep every non-expert tensor high: q8_0 (bf16 where the source is bf16 and the tensor is small). On both models this costs under 10 GiB.
evidence: Thireus per-tensor sweeps: attention/shared/dense tensors are about 100-5000x more sensitive per parameter than routed experts (GLM-5.1 attn_k_b 1.78 vs ffn_down_exps 0.0028 KLD per Gparam; Kimi K2-Thinking attn_kv_a_mqa 1.69 vs 0.0003)
Unsloth V3.1 Aider ablation: attn_k_b at 4-bit vs 8-bit cost about 2-3 points (chart read, approximate) for about 100 MB
QuantMoE-Bench: giving bits to attention beats giving them to FFN (>5% gain)
Unsloth GLM-5.3-Flash keeps all non-experts q8_0 down to UD-Q3_K_XL; ubergarm keeps q8_0/iq6_k at every tier

rules.rule: output.weight is the single most sensitive tensor: q8_0 or bf16, never below q6_K.
evidence: Thireus: dropping output.weight alone costs +0.542 PPL (V3.1) and +0.516 (R1-0528); the worst single expert layer costs 0.0345 / 0.0227
GLM-5.2 KLD 0.1248 for output.weight vs 0.0121 for the worst ffn_down_exps layer

rules.rule: Below about 2.6 bits average on the experts, coding and agent quality fall off a cliff; 1-bit gate/up is not for coding.
evidence: Unsloth GLM-5.3-Flash: top-1 70.89% (UD-IQ1_S) / 78.34% (UD-Q2_K_XL) / 86.25% (UD-Q3_K_XL) / 92.22% (UD-Q4_K_XL)
Unsloth V3.1 Aider Polyglot: 1-bit 55.7, 2-bit 65.8, 3-bit 68.4 (thinking 57.8 / 66.7 / 75.6), full model 71.6 / 76.1
Unsloth Kimi K3: mean KLD 0.5645 (UD-IQ1_S) vs 0.1779 (UD-Q2_K_XL)
Unsloth Dynamic 3.0: 1-bit quants are not for agentic or tool use

rules.rule: Shared experts and dense FFN layers stay at q8_0 (q6_K minimum); watch the last-layer shared expert.
evidence: Thireus V3.1: shared-expert sensitivity about 0.85 PPL per Gparam vs 0.005 for routed experts
Last-layer shared-expert outliers: R1 ffn_down_shexp layer 60 0.0972 vs median 0.0033; GLM-5.2 layers 75-76 1.072 vs median 0.0104
QuantMoE-Bench: shared experts need more bits (4 vs 2)

rules.rule: Give ffn_down_exps the gate/up type or one tier more; raising down is the cheapest expert upgrade.
evidence: ubergarm Kimi K2-Thinking: down iq2_kl -> iq3_ks moves PPL 2.4550 -> 2.3735 for 2.755 -> 2.920 bpw (Q4_X 2.0818)
ubergarm Kimi K2-Instruct 0.2: 3.4086 -> 3.1813; K2-0905: 2.9294 -> 2.7993 for the same change
Thireus: ffn_down_exps median sensitivity 1.1-1.3x gate or up alone
Unsloth keeps down at iq3_xxs (3.15 bpw) even in GLM-5.3-Flash UD-IQ1_S; mainline Q2_K raises down to q3_K

Counter-evidence: Unsloth Kimi K3 UD quants give down the same type as gate/up; Lucebox V4.1 fp3 down everywhere (179 GiB, KL 0.272) did not beat fp2s everywhere (158 GiB, KL 0.266), but the gate/up format also differed

rules.rule: Which layers get the extra bits is model-specific: measure per model, then spend bits on the sensitive layers. Measured allocation beats uniform types at the same size.
evidence: GLM-5.1/5.2 and Kimi K2-Thinking: early expert layers most sensitive (GLM-5.1 thirds 0.0155/0.0073/0.0036); DeepSeek V3.1/R1: middle-late layers (V3.1 thirds 0.0134/0.0248/0.0239)
V4.1 (Lucebox): fp3 down on layers 0-9 cut KL 0.266 -> 0.246, top-1 77.7% -> 78.3%, PPL 9.59 -> 9.45 for +6 GiB
V4 Flash (not V4.1): antirez Q4K on layers 37-42 cut KLD 0.4079 -> 0.3605 (86.7 -> 97.6 GB); KeinNiemand and Unsloth raise late layers
Thireus measured allocation vs uniform ubergarm smol-IQ2_KS at equal size: GLM-4.7 PPL 5.1061 vs 5.9716; Kimi K2-Thinking 2.8375 vs 2.9361; GLM-5.1 3.8394 vs 3.8818 (marginal)

rules.rule: Use an importance matrix from a chat and code corpus; it matters most at 2 bits and below.
evidence: antirez V4 Flash IQ2_XXS with vs without imatrix: KLD 0.4079 vs 0.4207, PPL 6.0808 vs 6.1518
Unsloth Dynamic 2.0/3.0 credit their gains partly to calibration data (>1.5M tokens chat, then agentic coding + multilingual)

rules.rule: DeepSeek V4/V4.1 experts are QAT MXFP4: at 4 bits keep native MXFP4 (lossless); requantizing them costs more than requantizing a bf16 model would.
evidence: Unsloth V4 Flash: UD-Q4_K_XL (MXFP4 experts) KLD 0.0102 vs antirez Q4KExperts 0.0291 at a larger size (155.1 vs 164.6 GB)
Unsloth: requant error about 5% for Q4_K and over 30% for IQ2_XXS

rules.rule: At equal bytes, ik iq/trellis types beat K-quants on quality; on our AVX2 CPUs K-quants decode about 1.6-3x closer to the memory ceiling. For CPU-resident experts a K-quant one tier up is the better trade; put iq types only on GPU-resident tensors until iq2_xxs/iq2_kl are measured on our boxes.
evidence: ik discussion 715 (R1-0528, Q8_0 3.2130): ik IQ2_KL recipe 2.930 bpw PPL 3.4379 vs Unsloth UD_Q2_K_XL 2.994 bpw 3.5278
Our measurement (brief): iq*_ks 0.31-0.54 of memory ceiling vs q2_K/q3_K/q4_K 0.87-0.95 on AVX2
Counter-evidence: ik PR 602 AVX2 tg-128 IQ2_KL 16.79 vs Q2_K 14.18 t/s (Ryzen 5975WX, Llama-8B)
Unsloth Qwen3.5 (GPU): K-quants 5-10% faster decode than iq types

rules.rule: Per-expert allocation by routing frequency works on unbalanced routing, but standard GGUF cannot express it: one type covers all experts of a layer and projection.
evidence: MC-MoE PMQ on Mixtral 8x7B at 2.54 bits: MMLU 61.19 vs Hessian 58.22 vs BSP 31.57 (16-bit 70.60)
QuantMoE-Bench: frequency heuristic fairly good, better on unbalanced routing; raising the top frequent experts from 4 to 8 bits adds little
buddalaw V4.1 K128/K160 domain-pruned: KLD 0.119 / 0.098 vs MXFP4 in domain, large loss out of domain

rules.rule: The MTP/nextn layer gets no imatrix data: quantize it with K-quants or q8_0, never iq types that need an imatrix.
evidence: Unsloth GLM-5.3-Flash uses q2_K/q3_K/q4_K on layer 45 inside otherwise iq quants; AesSedai uses q8_0; ubergarm iq5_ks on GLM-5.1 layer 78

rules.rule: V4.1 engram tables: nobody has published a quality measurement for any engram quant. Bandwidth cost is negligible (about 48 rows per token), so the type only decides capacity. token_embd, the closest analogue, is about 9-11x more sensitive per parameter than an expert layer, so do not drop engram below q5_K without a KLD test.
evidence: Engram types in the wild: raw FP8 + scales (JigSawPT, antirez), MXFP8 (SaturnHeaven, 188.8 GiB), q8_0 (vcruz, smalinin, pfeifferj), q5_K (smalinin, 135.172 GB pair vs 208.902 GB q8_0)
JigSawPT: tables are memory-mapped and read 48 rows per token; with too little page cache for them, decode slows
Thireus token_embd per Gparam vs ffn_down_exps: R1 0.0298 vs 0.0028; GLM-5.1 0.0255 vs 0.0028
